html:
The Battle of Chaeronea was fought in 338 BCE in Boeotia, central Greece, between Macedon under Philip II and an alliance of Greek cities led by Athens and Thebes. Macedon won, and Philip became master of Greece.

Demosthenes had brought Athens and Thebes together against Philip, and he fought in the battle himself. The two armies were about the same size. According to later accounts, Philip on the right drew the Athenians forward by pulling back, while his son Alexander, aged eighteen, led the cavalry on the left and broke through the Thebans. The Theban Sacred Band, an elite unit of three hundred, fought to the death. A great stone lion still marks the site, near a grave of about 250 skeletons thought to be theirs.

Philip treated Athens gently and Thebes harshly. The next year he gathered the Greek states into the League of Corinth, under his leadership, for a war on Persia. The age of the independent Greek city-state was over.
